newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner 9-mo oper profit up 29.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner 9-mo oper profit up 29.7 pct.

text.p: Nine months to September 30 (in millions of marks unless otherwise stated)
Group oper profit after provisions 1,891 vs 1,458
Group net bad debt provisions 857.2 up 9.7 pct

NOTE - Full name of the German bank is Dresdner Bank AG. Results compare with the first nine months of 1995. Analysts' forecasts for Dresdner's operating earnings ranged from 1.82 billion marks to 2.04 billion, with an average forecast of 1.95 billion, up 34 percent.

NOTE - Dresdner Bank said the integration of its merchant banking unit Kleinwort Benson had improved its commission income by around 25 percent and also boosted its interest income. Counting the integration of Kleinwort, administrative costs rose 4.9 percent in the period.
In a statement, Dresdner cited chief executive Juergen Sarrazin as saying end-of year trading income would rise at a double digit rate because pending earnings would by then be realised.
The increase in risk provisions in the first nine months was mainly due to allocations to cover business with medium sized domestic corporate clients.
Sarrazin also noted that earnings on its securities portfolio were "unusually high" at 605 million marks. The balance sheet total at end-September was 541 billion marks.
He said the bank planned measures to reduce its costs, and aimed to cut its costs/earnings ratio in its branch network to well below 70 percent. --Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
